misconception_diagnosis.justification: The tutor correctly identifies the 'measurement reveals a preexisting value' misconception and challenges it directly: turn 1 asks about repeated measurements, turn 2 argues the 50/50 split means measurement isn't 'simply revealing some pre-existing value,' and turn 3 names it as the 'pre-measurement vs post-measurement' issue and introduces collapse. Addresses the right misconception, though it does not validate up front why the single-axis statistics make the misconception so reasonable.

scaffolding_strategy.justification: Good question-driven progression matched to the calculus-level student: repeat-the-experiment probe, the random-walk analogy, then distinguishing eigenstates/bases. It builds toward the discriminating x-axis case. Slightly diluted by an overstatement (treating the +x state as '50/50 along z' as if z were special), but largely appropriate and responsive.

answer_disclosure_restraint.justification: Mixed: the tutor guides with questions but also asserts conclusions directly ('each measurement collapses the superposition... not because the electron was already in that state,' turn 3). On the transfer it walks through the 100%-x vs 50/50-z contrast itself before the student does. Some telling at key moments.

conceptual_model_building.justification: Builds the transferable model that a superposition is a genuine state (not ignorance), that measurement collapses it, and that complementary bases (z vs x) give different certainties — the lever the expert strategy identifies. Generalizes beyond the single measurement. Not a 4 because some framing (z as the privileged basis) is imprecise.

transfer_success.justification: On the x-measurement transfer the student correctly predicts the +x state gives spin-up along x with certainty while z gives 50/50, and concludes a single set of hidden up/down labels cannot produce both — so the electron had no definite z-value beforehand and measurement creates it. This meets the success criteria; the student articulates the contradiction in their own words.

pedagogical_harm_avoidance.justification: Physics is essentially correct (superposition vs ignorance, collapse, eigenstates, the falsifiable x-vs-z contrast), with only minor loose phrasing. Tone is encouraging and the student stays engaged and motivated. No misconception reinforced; harm avoided. Short of 4 because it does not maximally validate the student's productive partial intuition or note empirical (Bell) grounding cleanly.
